problem.text: The positive integers $N$ and $N^2$ both end in the same sequence of four digits $abcd$ when written in base $10$, where digit $a$ is not zero. Find the three-digit number $abc$.

steps.title: Where to start: turn "same last four digits" into a congruence
steps.body: The last four digits of a number are its remainder mod $10000$. So the statement says $N^2 \equiv N \pmod{10000}$, which means $10000$ divides $N^2 - N = N(N-1)$. Since $10000 = 2^4\cdot 5^4 = 16\cdot 625$ and $16$ and $625$ share no factor, we can handle the $16$ and the $625$ separately.

your_turn.prompt: Why can $N$ and $N - 1$ never both be even, or both be multiples of $5$?
your_turn.answer: They are consecutive, so any common divisor divides $N - (N-1) = 1$.

steps.title: Each prime power goes into one factor
steps.body: Because $N$ and $N-1$ share no factor of $2$, all of $16$ must divide one of them; likewise all of $625$ must divide one of them. That leaves four cases: $10000 \mid N$; $10000 \mid N - 1$; $16 \mid N$ and $625 \mid N-1$; or $625 \mid N$ and $16 \mid N-1$.

your_turn.prompt: What are the last four digits of $N$ in the first two cases, and why are those cases ruled out?
your_turn.answer: $0000$ and $0001$. In both the digit $a$ is $0$, but the problem says $a \neq 0$.

steps.title: Case: $625 \mid N$ and $16 \mid N - 1$
steps.body: Write $N = 625j$ for a whole number $j$. We need $625j \equiv 1 \pmod{16}$. Find the remainder of $625$ mod $16$ first; it makes this easy.

your_turn.prompt: Find $625 \bmod 16$, then the last four digits of $N$ in this case. Does it work?
your_turn.answer: $625 = 39\cdot 16 + 1$, so $j \equiv 1 \pmod{16}$ and $N \equiv 625 \pmod{10000}$. The last four digits are $0625$, so $a = 0$: this case fails.

steps.title: Case: $16 \mid N$ and $625 \mid N - 1$
steps.body: This is the only case left. Write $N = 1 + 625j$. We need $1 + 625j$ to be a multiple of $16$, and again $625 \equiv 1 \pmod{16}$ helps.

your_turn.prompt: Reduce $1 + 625j$ mod $16$. What condition on $j$ do you get?

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: With $j = 15$, $N \equiv 1 + 625\cdot 15 = 9376 \pmod{10000}$, so $abcd = 9376$ and $a = 9 \neq 0$. Check: $9376^2 = 87909376$, which also ends in $9376$. So $abc = 937$. The answer is **$937$**.
